outline.title: The Wrong Side
outline.premise: Commander Sera Voss awakens from a century-long cryogenic stasis to find the war she ignited has long since ended — and the enemy she despised, the Keth Collective, won. But the world they built from the ashes is clean, fed, and at peace, forcing Sera to confront the possibility that everything she fought and killed for was not only lost, but wrong.
themes: The moral cost of certainty in wartime
History written by survivors, not victors alone
The violence of ideology versus the patience of compassion

characters.name: Sera Voss
characters.role: Protagonist — former Commander of the Terran Sovereignty Forces
characters.arc: Moves from rigid, self-righteous soldier to a woman shattered and rebuilt by the truth of what her war actually cost.

characters.name: Davan Keth
characters.role: Archivist of the New Collective, great-grandchild of Sera's primary enemy
characters.arc: Begins as a cautious custodian of painful history and becomes an unlikely witness to Sera's reckoning, choosing mercy over justice.

characters.name: General Mira Voss
characters.role: Sera's sister, known only through historical records — she defected to the Keth mid-war
characters.arc: Present only as a ghost in the archive, her betrayal reframed as the bravest act in the conflict.

chapters.title: The Sleeper and the Ash
chapters.beat: Sera Voss is revived from a cryo-pod buried beneath a ruined Terran bunker by Davan Keth, who found her during an excavation, and she emerges armed, disoriented, and certain the war is still being fought.
chapters.arc_notes: Opening — world establishment and protagonist introduction; Sera's worldview is presented as absolute and unquestioned, the post-apocalyptic landscape revealed as unexpectedly green and ordered rather than devastated.

chapters.title: The Archive of Enemies
chapters.beat: Davan brings Sera to the Collective's living city and walks her through the historical archive, where she discovers her own war crimes documented in meticulous detail, and finds her sister Mira honored as a peacemaker who died trying to stop her.
chapters.arc_notes: Rising action — central conflict deepens as Sera's identity and moral framework collapse; the enemy is humanized and the protagonist is implicated; grief and rage compete inside her.

chapters.title: The Wrong Side
chapters.beat: Sera, given the choice by the Collective's council to be tried for war crimes or to record her own testimony for the archive, chooses testimony — and in speaking the truth aloud for the first time, she becomes the last honest monument to the war she started.
chapters.arc_notes: Climax and resolution — Sera does not receive forgiveness or punishment but something harder: witness; the turn is her choosing truth over pride; the ending is quiet, irreversible, and earned.
